hints.title: Algebraic Transformation of Index Difference
hints.text: The condition where j - i does not equal nums[j] - nums[i] is algebraically equivalent to nums[i] - i does not equal nums[j] - j.

hints.title: Counting Good Pairs
hints.text: A good pair satisfies nums[i] - i == nums[j] - j. Count frequencies of diff[i] = nums[i] - i across all indices.

hints.title: Complementary Subtraction
hints.text: Total possible pairs is n * (n - 1) // 2. Bad pairs equal total pairs minus good pairs.

hints.title: Frequency Complement Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def countBadPairs(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        total_pairs = n * (n - 1) // 2
        counts = Counter(x - i for i, x in enumerate(nums))
        good_pairs = sum(c * (c - 1) // 2 for c in counts.values())
        return total_pairs - good_pairs
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all pairs explicitly takes quadratic O(n^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counter stores frequency of unique (nums[i] - i) values.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Rewrites the equality to isolate variables to their own indices, using complement counting.
